entries.evidence: (1) Both losses are xe engine resets on GPU0 0000:0b:00.0: dmesg 'Tile0: GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs ... Timedout job ... in strata' at 19:30:57 and 19:55:07 local (17:30:57Z, 17:55:07Z); xe ccs job_timeout_ms = 5000. (2) RL-158 correction: its run-B 503/400 at ~17:31Z coincide with the 17:30:57Z engine reset; the systemd-oomd terminal kill came 9 minutes later (17:39:54Z). (3) Attempt 3 (RL-159, run-root above) was contaminated by the lead: four capped subagent CPU lanes ran beside it although the plan declared no co-scheduled CPU-heavy lane. Guard log: MemAvailable stayed ~32 GB but memory PSI full avg10 rose 0.0 -> 0.26 -> 3.65 -> 7.31 across t5/t6; the reset hit during t5-code-output; the guard aborted at t6:after (PSI > 5). Mechanism unproven: candidates are host-side feeder starvation of Strata's device-side waits beyond the 5 s job timeout, and eviction of the unlocked PLE table ('PLE table mlock failed ... pages may be reclaimed', --ple-io ram). entries.question: Forensics on the RQ-26 F0 harness (RL-150, RL-157): why were blocks blind, why did AutoRound diverge, and does the RL-151 'AutoRound-uniform beat EXL3 10-16x' reading survive?
entries.path_tried: Subagent forensic audit with capped CPU repros (MemoryMax=3G): rebuilt att_l03 from the sealed run's saved weights, channel attribution of block deltas and outputs, comparison of the homemade AutoRound loop with Intel auto-round source.
entries.evidence: (1) RL-151 CORRECTED: the AutoRound-uniform arms that read 0.06-0.10x EXL3 KL on att_l63 and gdn_l62 were stored at 8.125 bpw - every tensor escaped to INT8 (att_l63 7/7, gdn_l62 6/6), above the 4.5 bpw cap. The only INT4-pure AutoRound arm (gdn_l62 ar-e2m1, 4.125 bpw) was 12.7x WORSE than EXL3. No HQ4 arm showed EXL3-class quality at <= 4.5 bpw. (2) Metric blindness: one massive-activation channel (3994) holds 94-98 % of the block delta/output norm on the dead blocks; softmax over standardized channels is the same one-hot for reference and quantized arms (z-gap 50-67 nats), so a 14.5 % delta error reads KL -2.0e-20 (reproduced bit-for-bit, fp64 identical). (3) The homemade AutoRound optimized unbounded group clip scales with constant-lr Adam and returned the last state; Intel auto-round uses SignSGD on a bounded rounding offset, bounded min/max multipliers, lr decay and best-state export. All 48 traces rose monotonically. Recommended metric for any re-screen: fp32 relative Frobenius error of the block delta plus final-logit KL and next-token agreement.

entries.question: Why did both sealed RQ-25 isolated-screen attempts (RL-163, RL-164) fail, and did either measure the SoA layout mechanism?
entries.path_tried: Read raw bench stdout/stderr, cells.tsv and cell JSON of both runs, dmesg for 0000:0f:00.0, the bench source (rq25_bench.cpp, engine_iq3xxs_dev.dp.h) and run_bench.sh; reproduced the shell defect with `bash -c 'GROUPS=128; echo $GROUPS'` -> 1000.
entries.evidence: Neither attempt measured the mechanism; both are harness defects. (1) RL-163: the adapter ran the AOT binaries without the oneAPI runtime: 'libsycl.so.9: cannot open shared object file' before any cell. Fixed: adapter sources /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh (runtime 2026.1 = build toolchain). (2) RL-164: run_bench.sh assigned GROUPS=128, but GROUPS is a read-only bash special array; assignment is silently ignored and $GROUPS expands to the gid (1000). Both cell-words JSON record groups 1000 vs ring_slots 427. words cells passed (EmitLaunch ignores G); the first dots-E1 cell launched 1000 work-groups that dereferenced grp_ptr[427..999] past the 427-entry device table -> dmesg 20:24:57 'Engine memory CAT error [18] class=ccs' x6 -> engine reset -> UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST. Fixed: NGROUPS plus a ring_slots bound check before the first cell (scripts/tmp/rq25_soa_20261011/run_bench.sh:50-55). Earlier unsealed fixes the same day: parse_mode tail for warm-/timed- modes (rq25_bench.cpp:76), tag double-dash (run_bench.sh), missing RING/OUT/next_slice. (3) Unsealed GPU1 smoke at groups 128 (not a screen: one cell each, no pairs): logical GB/s aos128 178.4, aos256 212.5, soa256 214.4 (/mnt/<nvme-disk>/b70-run3-20261011/rq25-smoke2/). Single-cell lead only: SoA vs AoS at equal 256 GRF is +0.9%, the 128->256 GRF change is +19%; both far below the 1.5x gate. Not evidence for or against adoption.

entries.question: Do the RQ-17 xe engine resets (RL-160, RL-162) reproduce when Strata serves the frozen host tasks outside the battery adapter, on either card?
entries.path_tried: Unsealed diagnostic after RL-162: config of record with ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR level_zero:1 (GPU1) then level_zero:0 (GPU0, control), same image, pack and flags; client scripts/tmp/strata_reset_diag_20261011.py sends 1 warmup + the 10 frozen host tasks x 2 passes, records status, wall, usage, MemAvailable and PSI per request.
entries.evidence: 21/21 requests HTTP 200 on each card (42/42), zero xe resets in dmesg during either diagnostic; all 10 tasks returned the same content on both passes and both cards (e.g. t1 'cache-03', t2 '320', t3 '50', t8 '14', t9 '22.2'); PSI full avg10 0.0-1.16, MemAvailable ~35 GB with the server up. Contrast: RL-162 (attempt 4) reset 2 s into the FIRST warmup request after server ready (guard 18:04:52Z PSI 1.37, MemAvailable 33.9 GB; dmesg 20:04:54 local 'Timedout job ... in strata'); attempt 3 reset during t6-long-input-qa (PSI 3.65 before). The PSI spikes recorded after each reset coincide with server teardown (MemAvailable jumps back to ~53 GB), so cause and effect are not separated. Every Strata run on this host, including the passing RQ-14 screen, logged 'PLE table mlock failed (raise ulimit -l)'; the unlocked PLE table is the norm, not a difference. Conclusion: the reset is intermittent and not reproduced by the same requests on an idle host on either card; the card is not implicated (GPU1 clean too). Mechanism open: candidates are battery-adapter request timing (warmup immediately after ready), host page-cache churn while the 18 GiB pinned mirror fills, and the 5000 ms xe ccs job timeout.
entries.blocked_pattern: Do not attribute Strata engine resets to a specific card or to host memory pressure without a controlled reproduction; RQ-17 re-entry needs a named mechanism (e.g. a post-ready settle delay or raised ccs job timeout) tested unsealed first.

entries.question: Why did both sealed RQ-27 R0 attempts (RL-168, RL-169) fail, and what does the unsealed 13-layer prefix say about the R0 gate?
entries.path_tried: Read both sealed run roots, dmesg/journal, and ran one unsealed smoke quantizing the contiguous prefix layers 0-12 at full 64x512 calibration with 2x832 eval positions (same harness, same arms).
entries.evidence: Execution: attempt 1 (RL-168) lost positive-definiteness in the device blocked fp32 Cholesky at layer 11 after 10 clean layers. The same layer factorized fine in the unsealed prefix smoke, so the blocked path is non-deterministic at the PD boundary. Attempt 2 (RL-169) added a classic fp64 CPU fallback; the blocked path failed earlier, at L2 gptq_plain mlp.down_proj, the fp64 fallback took 33.3 s, and the 17408x17408 fp64 working set exceeded the 14 GiB container cap: kernel oom-kill CONSTRAINT_MEMCG at 22:31:42, rc 137. Neither attempt scored an arm. Quality signal (unsealed, not a verdict; prefix 0-12 quantized, 1664 eval positions): final-logit KL vs bf16 exl3 0.00122 (top-1 0.969), gptq_plain 0.00438 (0.942), r4_g128 0.00411 (0.939), r4_g64 0.00353 (0.944); r4_fp 0.00013. The best R4 arm sits at 2.9x EXL3's KL; rotation recovers 6 % (G128) and G64 a further 14 % of plain GPTQ's KL. The 2-layer smoke showed the same order (RL-167). Fold exact on every probed layer (rel L2 1.3-1.6e-6).
entries.blocked_pattern: Residual-stream Hadamard rotation plus symmetric GPTQ INT4 does not approach EXL3 trellis quality on Qwen3.8-27B in a 13-layer prefix (2.9x KL); do not re-run R0 without a new quantizer mechanism (e.g. learned rotation, vector/trellis codebook) or an fp64-on-device hinv with a >= 24 GiB container cap.

entries.question: Close RQ-27 (R4 residual-rotated INT4): what killed it, and what replaces it?
entries.path_tried: Lead review of RL-167..RL-170 plus rate-distortion arithmetic, and an adversarial review lane (local format-review, GPT 6 Astra) of the explanation.
entries.evidence: Quality, not speed, killed R4. Unsealed 13-layer prefix: r4_g64 KL 0.00353 vs EXL3 0.00122 (2.9x). Two candidate causes, both live: (a) fixed-rate scalar grid: uniform 4-bit on a Gaussian has MSE 0.01154 vs D(4 bits) = 2^-8 = 0.0039 (2.95x), Lloyd-Max 2.43x, while EXL3 is a QTIP-family trellis near D(R); (b) R4's fold is one-sided per linear: down_proj and o_proj inputs and their Hessians were never rotated (review finding). Speed was never the problem: the stock INT4 path measured 1.62x EXL3 decode on the old image (RQ-27 economic gate). Both sealed attempts died on harness defects (RL-168, RL-169). Successor RQ-28 adds int4_g64_rht (two-sided incoherence, scalar) to separate (a) from (b), and tests E8P lattice RVQ at 4.0 bpw.
entries.blocked_pattern: Residual-stream (one-sided) Hadamard fold plus scalar GPTQ INT4 on Qwen3.8-27B: do not re-run without a two-sided incoherence or non-scalar quantizer.

entries.question: Was R4's 2.9x KL gap caused by one-sided incoherence or by the scalar grid itself, and can E8 lattice RVQ close it at 4.0 bpw?
entries.path_tried: Unsealed 13-layer prefix screen (layers 0-12, 64x512 calibration, 1664 eval positions) with deterministic fp32 hinv (52/52 factor pairs torch.equal): arms bf16, exl3, r4_g64 (one-sided fold), int4_g64_rht and int4_g128_rht (per-linear two-sided block-128 sign-Hadamard + GPTQ sym INT4). CPU Monte Carlo of E8P12 2-stage RVQ (per-row scales) vs D(R).
entries.evidence: Final-logit KL vs bf16 (top-1, r01 margin): exl3 0.00122 (0.9675, +1.246); r4_g64 0.00358 (0.9447, +1.135) = 2.93x; int4_g64_rht 0.00301 (0.9567, +1.178) = 2.46x; int4_g128_rht 0.00348 (0.9495, +1.204) = 2.84x. Full two-sided incoherence recovers 16 % of the G64 gap; the rest is the fixed-rate scalar grid: Gaussian Monte Carlo uniform INT4 2.955x D(4), Lloyd-Max 2.432x, matching the measured KL ratios. E8P12 2-stage RVQ with per-row scales: Gaussian MSE 9.24e-3 = 2.37x D(4), only ~1.25x better than uniform scalar (plain infinite E8 lattice 1.22x; the loss is codebook and scale side information). E8RVQ4 cannot reach EXL3 (trellis class ~1.1x D(R)); no GPU time spent on it. Conclusion: at 4.0 bpw on this model only a trellis-class quantizer matches EXL3; recipe changes to scalar INT4 cannot.
entries.blocked_pattern: Fixed-rate scalar INT4 (any rotation, G64/G128, GPTQ) and E8P RVQ at 4.0 bpw on Qwen3.8-27B: both sit >= 2.3x the rate-distortion bound; do not screen again without a trellis-class or entropy-coded quantizer.

entries.question: XTQ K2/K3: is there a trellis code with near-EXL3 distortion at K=4 whose Xe2 decode costs >= 1.4x fewer issues per weight?
entries.path_tried: CPU tail-biting Viterbi (L=16, 256-weight sequences, 2048 sequences, i.i.d. Gaussian) for EXL3 mul1 (bit-exact vs ref.py, torch.equal on a full tensor), QTIP 1MAD/3INST/HYB, EXL3 mcg, and five Xe2-native candidates (V=1 and byte-aligned V=2); BMG AOT compile with ocloc disassembly of decode kernels, 128 GRF, 0 spills.
entries.evidence: K2 MSE/D(4): EXL3 mul1 1.178x RD (K=2: 0.0701 = 1.12x, matching QTIP Table 1). Within the 1.05x kill line: mcg 1.027x, 1MAD 1.028x, 3INST 1.041x of EXL3 (all V=1, same decode cost class). Fail: xe_ih2x2 1.099x, xe_bs2 1.157x, xe_hyb10 1.254x, qtip_hyb 1.31x, xe_u2 4.46x. K3 decode issue per 512 B: EXL3 ~85.5 (0.334/weight); xe_u2 ~49 (1.74x less), xe_ih2x2 ~50 (1.71x), xe_hyb10 ~57 (1.49x), qtip_hyb ~58 (1.47x), xe_bs2 ~68 (fail). Joint gate empty: the V=2 byte-aligned decode point is cheap because one 8-bit symbol commits a weight pair, which costs a 1.06-1.3x distortion floor (tables up to Q=13 reach 1.063x). Nearest candidate xe_ih2x2: +9.9 % MSE (~0.07 bit) for 1.71x cheaper decode (0.195 issues/weight vs the 0.206 needed for pin rate).

entries.question: Does MiaAI's Engine-Aware Quantization (EAQ) or the TensorFold engine offer anything better than our EXL3 routes (plain 4.00bpw, SC_5.00bpw_H6), and should TensorFold be ported to the B70?

entries.evidence: EAQ: unpublished and in validation; the tweet says 37 % lower KL vs stock EXL3 while the page says 41 %/54 % lower undefined 'error' vs the author's own quant; target is MoE GLM-5.3-Flash. The predecessor quant measured 2-18 % lower KL as served vs FP8, and most of the served error is TensorFold's load-time q4 dense requantization (floor 0.0676 of 0.0903 wiki), the error EAQ calibrates around; exl3xpu does no such requantization. A workload-matched held-out evaluation would not have caught SC4's prose regression (RL-179: chat 0.75x, prose 1.15x). Taken at face value EAQ would be ~0.63x plain KL, still worse than SC5 (0.42x/0.16x). TensorFold 1.0.9: Zig engine, Metal + CUDA kernels only, no SYCL/Level Zero; Qwen3.8-27B qualified on Metal only and slower than mlx_lm without the drafter; SC5 no-spec is at 99.5 % of its byte floor (RL-202), so an engine swap has no raw-decode headroom.

entries.question: Is the run-to-run drift of int8-prefill SC5 outputs (RL-212/213) caused by a non-deterministic prefill kernel, and would making int8 prefill deterministic remove its quality cost?
entries.path_tried: Isolated op probes in ghcr.io/sergiiob/exl3xpu-mixedk@sha256:933eda54 on GPU1, 30 bitwise repeats each (cloned outputs, integer-view compare): E.linear int8 and fp16 on real SC5 tensors K=4..7 at M=1024/600; torch.matmul fp16; oneDNN Graph SDPA (exl3_sdpa_len) and vllm_xpu_kernels FA2 at Q=1024 with and without a 1024-token prefix; FLA chunk_gated_delta_rule T=1024 cold and with initial state. Amplification: 0.1 % of inputs nudged one fp16 ulp. Source grep for atomics.
entries.evidence: Every probed op is bitwise deterministic (0/29 mismatching repeats each). No atomics in FLA/GDN, causal_conv1d or FA paths; the only exl3xpu atomic is a completion counter in fused_had_out with fixed-order reduction (decode path). One-ulp perturbation: fp16 linear amplification ~11.9, int8 ~23-26 (about 2x). So the serving drift is small input differences between requests upstream of the probed ops, amplified by int8 rounding. A deterministic int8 path would freeze one realization of the same rounding error: its distance to fp16 stays ~0.001 KL. The 'deterministic int8' lever proposed in research/2026/asserved-kl-and-eaq-tensorfold-20261014.md is withdrawn as a quality fix.
entries.validation_scope: isolated ops, one card; the upstream request-to-request input difference is not located
entries.blocked_pattern: making int8 prefill deterministic as a fix for its quality cost
